title: Build the machine, then map it to the edge
objective: Complete the official Nand2Tetris ALU and Memory projects, then write a five-row map from Hack machine constructs to a named MCU or QEMU target.
whyThisMatters: Registers, addressable memory, and a clocked instruction cycle are not abstractions you can skip on an edge node. If you cannot point at the corresponding parts of a real MCU, later MMIO and isolation work will be folklore.
evidence: Captured official Nand2Tetris test-script output showing Project 2 (ALU) and Project 3 (Memory) passing
The HDL (or official project files) committed with incremental history, not one final dump
EDGE-MAP.md with five named Hack constructs each paired to a named MCU or QEMU construct and one sentence of mechanism
A written fetch-decode-execute note listing what is read and written in each step
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The official Nand2Tetris test scripts for Project 2 (ALU) and Project 3 (Memory) are shown passing in a captured log; the log names the test files.

EDGE-MAP.md contains exactly five rows: register, RAM, ROM, instruction word, and clock — each row names one Hack construct and one corresponding construct on a named MCU family (for example Cortex-M0) or QEMU machine, plus one sentence of mechanism.
The fetch-decode-execute note lists those three steps as separate paragraphs and, for each step, names at least one location that is read and at least one location that is written.
Git history contains at least two commits that change HDL or project files before the final passing run.
